# Executive Summary

ISO/IEC 27001 provides the requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an information security management system (ISMS). It enables organisations to manage information security risks systematically and to demonstrate that information security is governed through a structured management system.

This document provides a practical template for defining the organisation’s ISO/IEC 27001 governance model, ISMS scope, risk management approach, control structure, implementation roadmap, and assurance model. It can be used to document how the organisation aligns information security governance, risk treatment, controls, and continual improvement into a coherent operating model.

# Overview

## Purpose

This document provides a practical template for defining, implementing, operating, and assuring an information security management system aligned to ISO/IEC 27001.

## Objectives

The main objectives of applying ISO/IEC 27001 are to:

-   establish a formal and auditable information security management system
-   protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information
-   align information security with business objectives and enterprise risk
-   apply systematic risk assessment and risk treatment
-   define and maintain appropriate information security controls
-   provide evidence of governance, monitoring, and continual improvement
-   support internal assurance and external certification where required

## Scope

Describe the scope of ISO/IEC 27001 applicability in the organisation.

### In scope

-   the defined ISMS boundary
-   business units, processes, and services within scope
-   information assets and supporting technology
-   applications, infrastructure, platforms, and cloud services
-   people, facilities, and third parties relevant to the ISMS
-   security governance, risk treatment, and control monitoring activities
-   incident management, resilience, and continual improvement activities within the ISMS scope

### Out of scope

Document justified exclusions, if any.

## Intended Audience

-   Board and executive leadership
-   Chief Information Security Officer
-   Chief Information Officer
-   Enterprise Risk Management teams
-   Security governance, architecture, and operations teams
-   IT operations and service management teams
-   Business owners and control owners
-   Compliance and legal teams
-   Internal audit and assurance teams
-   PMO / transformation teams

# Standard Foundation

## Background

ISO/IEC 27001 is the world’s best-known standard for information security management systems and specifies the requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an ISMS. It is designed to support a risk-based approach that can be scaled to organisations of different sizes and sectors. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index="1"}

## ISMS Principles

Document how the organisation applies the core principles of the ISMS:

-   risk-based thinking
-   leadership and accountability
-   information protection based on business needs
-   systematic control selection
-   evidence-based management
-   continual improvement
-   integration with organisational processes and governance

## Core Components

Describe the core components of the ISO/IEC 27001 model:

-   organisational context
-   leadership and policy
-   planning
-   support
-   operation
-   performance evaluation
-   improvement
-   information security risk assessment
-   information security risk treatment
-   Statement of Applicability

## Relationship to ISO/IEC 27002 and Annex A

Describe how the organisation uses:

-   ISO/IEC 27001 for management system requirements
-   Annex A as the information security controls reference
-   ISO/IEC 27002:2022 for guidance on information security controls

ISO states that ISO/IEC 27001 contains the ISMS requirements, while ISO/IEC 27002 provides detailed control guidance. ISO material and SC 27 guidance also explain that Annex A is a normative reference set of controls that must be considered as part of risk treatment and comparison for completeness. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index="2"}

### Example standards table

| Standard / Component | Purpose |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| ISO/IEC 27001 | Defines ISMS requirements |
| Annex A | Reference set of information security controls |
| ISO/IEC 27002 | Guidance on the implementation and management of controls |
| Statement of Applicability | Documents selected, excluded, and justified controls |

# Governance Model

## Governance Objectives

Define the governance objectives for ISO/IEC 27001 adoption:

-   establish executive accountability for information security
-   define the ISMS scope and governance boundary
-   align security priorities with enterprise strategy and risk appetite
-   assign ownership for risk treatment and control performance
-   embed information security into operations, change, architecture, and supplier management
-   maintain evidence of implementation and operating effectiveness
-   support continual improvement through monitoring, review, corrective action, and audit

## Governance Structure

Describe the governance bodies and their responsibilities.

### Example governance bodies

-   Board / Risk Committee
-   Executive Information Security Steering Committee
-   Information Security Forum
-   Enterprise Risk Committee
-   Architecture Review Board
-   Change Advisory Board
-   Internal Audit

## Three Lines Model

Describe responsibilities across the three lines.

### First line

-   ownership of business processes, assets, and operational controls
-   execution of security controls
-   risk treatment implementation
-   evidence production and remediation execution

### Second line

-   information security governance
-   policy and standard setting
-   risk oversight
-   compliance monitoring
-   challenge and advisory support

### Third line

-   internal audit
-   independent assurance
-   control effectiveness review

# Core Processes

## Context and Scope Management

Describe how the organisation determines and maintains:

-   internal and external issues
-   interested parties and their requirements
-   the ISMS scope statement
-   interfaces and dependencies
-   applicability boundaries

## Risk Assessment

Describe the process for:

-   defining risk criteria
-   identifying information security risks
-   assessing likelihood and impact
-   evaluating risks against criteria
-   prioritising treatment actions
-   documenting results

## Risk Treatment

Describe the process for:

-   selecting treatment options
-   determining necessary controls
-   comparing selected controls with Annex A
-   documenting inclusions and exclusions
-   assigning owners and due dates
-   approving residual risk
-   tracking treatment implementation

## Statement of Applicability

Document how the organisation maintains the Statement of Applicability, including:

-   selected controls
-   excluded controls
-   reasons for inclusion or exclusion
-   implementation status
-   associated policies or procedures
-   accountable owners

## Sample Control Catalogue

| Control ID | Control Name | Objective | Control Owner | Frequency | Evidence |
|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|------------|
| ISO-01 | ISMS policy approved | Ensure formal leadership direction | CISO | Annual | Approved policy |
| ISO-02 | Risk assessment performed | Identify and evaluate security risks | Risk Manager | Annual / change-driven | Risk assessment records |
| ISO-03 | Statement of Applicability maintained | Document selected and excluded controls | Security Governance Lead | Annual / change-driven | SoA |
| ISO-04 | Internal audit completed | Validate ISMS conformance and effectiveness | Audit Lead | Annual | Audit reports |
| ISO-05 | Management review performed | Ensure leadership oversight and decisions | Executive Sponsor | Annual | Management review minutes |
| ISO-06 | Corrective actions tracked | Improve nonconformity resolution | ISMS Manager | Ongoing | Action tracker |

# Implementation Roadmap

## Maturity Phases

### Phase 1: Foundation

-   define organisational context and ISMS scope
-   establish governance and executive sponsorship
-   approve core policy framework
-   define risk assessment and treatment methods
-   build initial asset inventory and baseline controls

### Phase 2: Control Design

-   perform risk assessment
-   create risk treatment plan
-   develop Statement of Applicability
-   implement priority control improvements
-   establish incident, supplier, and monitoring processes

### Phase 3: Integration

-   embed ISMS into change, architecture, procurement, and operations
-   improve evidence collection and monitoring
-   establish internal audit and management review cycle
-   align corrective action tracking with enterprise governance

### Phase 4: Optimisation

-   refine metrics and dashboards
-   strengthen automation and control monitoring
-   improve management review quality
-   enhance assurance readiness and continual improvement
-   support certification maintenance where applicable

# Maturity Model

## Suggested Maturity Levels

### Level 1: Initial

Security activities are reactive, fragmented, and poorly governed.

### Level 2: Repeatable

Basic ISMS components exist but are inconsistently applied and weakly evidenced.

### Level 3: Defined

The ISMS scope, policies, risk treatment, and controls are documented and broadly implemented.

### Level 4: Managed

The ISMS is measured, reviewed, audited, and actively improved through leadership oversight.

### Level 5: Optimised

Information security is fully integrated into enterprise governance, architecture, operations, and supplier management with strong evidence and continual improvement.
